messages:
leah: FYI we discovered a 10m gap (2026-03-20 22:00-22:10 UTC) that never landed in hourly aggregates. Thinking about running micro-catchups (delta replays) instead of a full shard backfill. pros/cons? :thinking_face:

sam: What's the raw event count for that slice? if it's small we can use delta-path and avoid reprocessing huge state. remember quota implications. :money_with_wings:

leah: Total ~48k events cluster-wide, but concentrated on two high-value routes/tenants. Cost estimate unclear because current replayer charges per-record in some aggregator paths.

priya: We already prototyped a prefix-aware stitch in staging last quarter. If we expose a delta-only replay endpoint that uses kv-stitch, we can skip full aggregators and only upsert affected keys. That reduces cost but needs strict idempotency guarantees.

mike: Console needs to surface a "micro-catchup" mode with an estimated cost + ETA before users hit run. Today the console only shows full-backfill estimates which are scary. UI option: "affected windows only" vs "full shard".

joan: Agree. Also ops: make sure these tiny jobs don't get preempted by reserved-capacity policies. Even small jobs currently consume tenant slots and can fail mid-run, leaving partial aggregates.

tim: For operators, here's the dry-run I used in staging:```bash
replayer --mode=delta --start=2026-03-20T22:00:00Z --end=2026-03-20T22:10:00Z --tenant=acme --shard=04 --dry-run
```It prints an estimator summary (token reads, rows, mem).

priya: If we ship delta endpoint, require a metadata contract: idempotency token + `catchup_reason` tag for downstream billing/QA. propose: catchup_reason=late_ingest_microwindow.

leah: Ops-bot, can you run a low-prio estimator dry-run on prod-sim and paste numbers? want to validate UI cost gauge before adding toggle.

ops-bot: deploybot: queued dry-run (delta) for window 2026-03-20T22:00Z-22:10Z on prod-sim. job id: job-20260320-522. ETA ~25s.

ops-bot: deploybot: dry-run complete. estimator: rows: "~1.9k", token_reads: "~118k", est_cost_usd: "0.31", peak_mem_mb: "600". (staging estimator output)

sam: $0.31 per micro-catchup seems fine. Main concern: concurrent micro-catchups could hit quota. UI should auto-group adjacent tiny windows into a single micro-batch and cap concurrency.

mike: UX idea: when selecting multiple nearby windows, auto-group into a micro-batch and show a concurrency slider (1-4). Default 1. Show combined ETA + combined cost. Include an inline warning if estimated concurrency breaches tenant slot quota.

joan: Scheduler requirements: micro-batch runner must honor reserved lanes and when capacity unavailable, degrade to fallback pool (lower-priority) rather than fail. Track preemptions and emit telemetry; alert if >5% preempted.

priya: API design debate: add "/v2/replay/delta" vs a "?delta=true" param on "/v1/replay". I prefer "/v2/replay/delta" to separate guarantees and route to specialized workers.

tim: v2 is cleaner. We can route v2 traffic to a small-window-optimized pool with lighter kernels and cheaper memory paths, avoiding interference with big backfills.

leah: Action items: 1) ops run non-prod dry-runs for a few tenants and paste estimator outputs (sam/tim) 2) product/ux (mike) mock console micro-catchup toggle and grouping behavior 3) platform (priya) write spec for "/v2/replay/delta" + tagging + idempotency 4) SRE (joan) define scheduler preemption fallback and alerts. I'll schedule 30m sync tomorrow.

sam: I'll add a quota check into the estimator so the UI can disable the micro-toggle if it would exceed concurrent slot limits.

mike: I'll put an initial mock in Figma and link here: https://go.redwood/ux/micro-catchup-mock (will update when ready).

priya: Ops suggestion: add a safety cap `max_affected_tenants` per micro-batch (default 3) to prevent a single-tenant spike creating many tiny jobs.

joan: +1 on tenant cap. Also ensure emitted telemetry includes `catchup_reason` so billing and QA queries can filter runs. Ops will prepare a saved dashboard to monitor micro-catchup failures and preemptions.

leah: Great. I'll send the sync invite and an agenda (dry-run numbers, API spec draft, UX mock). Thanks all.
